scope: Eight included authoritative-workbook records naming Uganda; six have named crossings. Identity review only, separate from geometry verification and chronology adjudication.
review_method: Same-model AI source review of substantive reporting; no human or independent-model validation.

sources.title: Confusion at Rwanda-Uganda border crossing after reopening
supports: GL01 names Katuna/Gatuna as the affected crossing; observed truck movement and continuing passenger restrictions
sources.notes: Original AFP reporting and attributed government comments. The reopening was category-specific; this source does not establish uninterrupted all-traffic closure.
sources.access: Substantive article text read in this review

sources.title: Nord-Kivu : interdiction d’importer et d’exporter les marchandises via Bunagana
supports: GL12 prohibition names Bunagana border post between DRC and Uganda
sources.notes: Reports the North Kivu governor’s signed 20 June communiqué prohibiting goods import/export through Bunagana. A reported legal prohibition is distinct from an observed physical seal; the government document itself was not newly obtained.
sources.access: Substantive article text read in this review

sources.title: Uganda reopens border posts with DR Congo
supports: GL13 explicitly names Bunagana and Ishasha
sources.notes: Reports military assistant Chris Magezi’s statement about the two crossings. This is attributed reporting of a directive and reopening; first ordinary passage at each post is not independently established.
sources.access: Substantive article text read in this review

sources.title: Uganda reopens border posts with eastern DRC
sources.publisher: Xinhua and Uganda Radio Network / The Independent
supports: GL13 names Bunagana, Ishasha and Busanza; identifies Busanza–Kitagoma
sources.notes: Reports a telephone interview with military spokesperson Felix Kulayigye and Bunagana ceremony. The instruction includes Busanza; this does not establish first physical traffic there. Name is Busanza–Kitagoma in Kisoro, not a same-name settlement by Ishasha.
sources.access: Substantive article text read in this review

sources.title: Nimule border closes temporarily as gunmen kill 2 police officers – Police
supports: R3-AF-006 identifies the South Sudan–Uganda border in Nimule
sources.notes: Direct interview with the Nimule police chief; photo caption identifies the bridge connection. Both sides’ closure is the officer’s account, not separate observations.
sources.access: Substantive article text read in this review

sources.title: Nimule border reopened after brief closure
supports: R3-AF-006 identifies the same international crossing and reported traffic resumption
sources.notes: Interviews the same principal police source as Eye Radio. It is corroborating publication, not an independent operational witness.
sources.access: Substantive article text read in this review

sources.title: Trucks Pile at Elegu Border Following Violence In South Sudan
supports: R3-AF-007 pairs Elegu in Amuru with Nimule, and describes halted road transport and customs clearance
sources.notes: The same URN article contains conflicting accounts: anonymous border staff say URA stopped clearing trucks, while named UPDF spokesperson Cpt Hassan Ahmed Kato says the Ugandan border remained open and operational. Crossing identity and the Nimule road disruption are supported; Ugandan formal closure is contested. Backlog and voluntary waiting after traffic resumed are separate.
sources.access: Substantive article text read in this review

sources.title: Truck drivers at Kenya-Uganda border on strike over Covid-19 tests
supports: R4-AES-002 is Malaba road freight entering Uganda from Kenya; rail is not established
sources.notes: Reports truck stoppage at Malaba with dated photo and interviews. Busia and opposite-direction traffic are reported separately. This review accepts location and movement identity only; it does not re-adjudicate conflicting onset or reopening reports.
sources.access: Substantive article text read in this review

sources.title: Uganda travel advice: Regional risks
supports: Identifies Kitagoma–Buszana as a crossing in Kisoro district
sources.notes: Geographic identity context only; current travel advice does not establish the closure dates or an OSM coordinate. The source spelling is Buszana; the closure report spells Busanza.

links.scope: Ugandan formal suspension at Busanza, until reopening permission.
links.phase_dates_policy: Retain authoritative workbook phase dates and qualifications; no date amendment or transfer to other crossings.
links.notes: Use the Busanza–Kitagoma crossing in Kisoro. Do not assign homonymous settlements near Bunagana or Ishasha. limitations: Verified_identity means that freshly read reporting connects the event to the named crossing, not that a particular OSM point has been verified.
All canonical workbook dates, scope, uncertainty and event data remain unchanged. This is not a new full chronology verification.
Source reports of official permission and reactivation cannot establish first ordinary passage or uninterrupted physical closure.

The source set combines original reporting, attributed official statements and syndicated reporting. Multiple publications using the same operational source are not counted as independent confirmation.
A nearby settlement name is discovery context only. Alternative roads and informal routes can be affected by a broader restriction without being the named formal crossing.
No national policy is expanded into assumed post-specific closure links. No link is published to the public-facing map in this work package.
